name: Gastroschisis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and imaging diagnosis of gastroschisis

criteria.description: Presence of a full-thickness paraumbilical abdominal wall defect with evisceration of intestines
Eviscerated bowel is not covered by a protective sac or membrane
Prenatal ultrasound showing free-floating bowel loops in amniotic fluid adjacent to the fetal abdomen

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of a paraumbilical abdominal wall defect with eviscerated bowel without a covering sac
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is often made prenatally via ultrasound or immediately after birth on physical examination.

imaging: Prenatal ultrasound showing free-floating bowel loops outside the abdominal cavity
Postnatal abdominal X-ray confirming abdominal wall defect and bowel position
genetic: No consistent genetic mutations identified; mostly sporadic cases
other: Physical examination revealing paraumbilical abdominal wall defect with exposed intestines

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of a protective sac covering the herniated abdominal contents
Midline abdominal wall defect at the base of the umbilical cord
Severe body wall defects with multiple anomalies
Often associated with limb and craniofacial abnormalities

redFlags: Signs of bowel ischemia or necrosis
Severe feeding intolerance or failure to establish enteral feeding
Signs of sepsis or systemic infection
references: Moore KL, Persaud TVN. The Developing Human: Clinically Oriented Embryology. 11th ed. Elsevier; 2015.
American Pediatric Surgical Association. Gastroschisis Clinical Practice Guidelines. 2020.
